Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short note on packaging options for the Optimize toolkit (batching/caching guidance + quantization recommendations) and what a pragmatic pilot credit structure could look like while you validate latency/quality tradeoffs.

High level proposal:
- 3-month pilot: access to Optimize features + dedicated onboarding hours
- Pilot credit: $25k of usage credits + 10k tokens of diagnostic evals included
- Optional add-on: quantization advisory (one-week consult) + model vetting for $8k

Before I send a formal quote, two asks so we can tighten the economics:
1) Do you expect most inference to be short-chat flows (<=256 tokens) or long prompts (>1k tokens)? It changes batching gains.
2) Are you open to an int8 quantization path on the models we serve, or do you require full FP16/FP32 fidelity for now?

I attached a one-pager and a short slide deck that show expected cost delta across three usage profiles. Marcus is looped for SOW and pricing.

Next step: if you can confirm the above, I’ll update the MAP and return a DocuSign-ready quote.

Thanks —
Aisha

- We need a one-page summary of what telemetry/audit logs are available and retention windows for the pilot.

Cc’ing Kevin (procurement) who will coordinate contract flow.

Ellen, quick technical context to set expectations on savings and fidelity:  

1) Batching: With ~70% short interactions, continuous small-batch aggregation should deliver 25–40% token-cost savings on hosted inference while retaining sub-200ms tail latency for single-turn responses. Savings scale with request concurrency and predictable prompt shapes.

2) Caching (prefix & KV): For repeated system prompts and common completions we typically see additional 8–15% token-cost reduction; for multi-turn chat with repeated context it can be higher. Cache hit-rate is the lever here — we can run a two-week collector job during pilot at no extra charge to estimate hit-rate.

3) Quantization: For the model class we looked at (open-chat-XXL-ish), int8 quantization typically adds a small quality delta; in our benchmarks summary tasks showed ~0.8–1.3% metric drift vs FP16, but this varies by prompt and instruction tuning. We recommend a two-track pilot:
  - Track A: int8 inference on non-critical routes (search, assistant small-talk) — validated immediately
  - Track B: shadow int8 outputs for summarization with automated quality checks (ROUGE/BLEU + a small human-review panel) before shifting production traffic.

4) Operational: Audit logs and token-level traces are available; default retention is 90 days for pilot tenants and can be extended. SOC2 report and pen-test evidence are available via our partner portal (I’ll add links).

Happy to run the collector job and a short quantization validation run next week.

—Sean

Option 2 — Pilot + Advisory (expedited validation)

- If you convert within 90 days, advisory fee is credited back at 50% toward year-one committed spend.

Notes: both options include standard MAP milestones (collector run, quantization shadow validation, 2-week quality panel). SLA/enterprise add-ons priced separately.

If that structure looks reasonable I’ll prepare a DocuSign-ready quote and update the HubSpot deal (VD-2026-0421).
